newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani rupee ends down in kerb, seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani rupee ends down in kerb, seen falling.

text.p: The Pakistani rupee ended 0.20 lower at 42.10 to the dollar in the kerb market on Monday on higher demand for the U.S. currency whose supplies fell sharply owing to the year-end holiday season, dealers said.
The rupee was likely to open lower on Tuesday, dealer Owais Kalia of Khanani and Kalia International (pvt) Ltd said.
The State (central) bank of Pakistan rate, last changed on October 22, was 40.1200/40.3206 rupees to the dollar.
The premium on foreign exchange bearer certificates closed at 5.20 percent, compared to the opening at 4.60 percent.
